exposure: Pre-pregnancy Body Mass Index (BMI) categorized into underweight (<18.5 kg/m2), normal (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), overweight (23.0-24.9 kg/m2), class I obesity (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), and class II/III obesity (>= 30.0 kg/m2)
outcome: Preterm delivery caused by maternal-fetal indications
cohort: The study included 6,331 Korean pregnant women from 12 institutions.
finding: A higher pre-pregnancy BMI, particularly starting from >= 23.0 kg/m2 (overweight by stricter Asian criteria), significantly increased the risk of preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm delivery, large for gestational age, and neonatal intensive care unit admission after adjusting for maternal age.
mod_finding: The risk of cesarean section significantly increased with a higher pre-pregnancy BMI.
